description: Use it when the user wants Product Hunt gallery images and thumbnail, an og:image, an X post image, a Google Play feature graphic or Chrome Web Store tiles. Makes the pictures a launch needs at the exact size each place asks for, as opaque PNGs in stills/, listed in STILLS.md, which the result shows. ph makes ph-1.png (the logo, the promise and the screen) and up to 5 of the film's scenes from ph-2.png on, all 1270x760, and ph-thumbnail.png at 240x240; og makes og.png at 1200x630; x makes x.png at 1600x900; play makes play-feature.png at 1024x500, Google Play's feature graphic only; chrome makes chrome-small.png at 440x280 and chrome-marquee.png at 1400x560. The words and the look come from a film.json, the logo from the brand and the screen from the site; no picture is 9:16. Given a site instead of a film.json, it plans a film first with the default look, length and aspect. For App Store or Google Play screenshots, use take_screenshots instead. The launch-film playbook (makersmcp_playbook) has the whole job. (launch-film 0.3.1, on this machine.)

for.description: Which places to make pictures for (default all of them): ph, the Product Hunt gallery and thumbnail; og, a link preview; x, a post on X; play, the Google Play feature graphic; chrome, the Chrome Web Store tiles.

out_dir.description: Folder to save into, absolute or relative to /tmp/churn-hnvpfmca. Default: launch-film-<host>, where <host> is the site's host without www or the port. A run replaces the files an earlier run of this kit left there, so give each version its own out_dir. Given a file instead of an address, the kit saves in the folder of source and takes no out_dir. The kit deletes the brand/ folder in it and makes it again for an App Store page, so it does not start then while that folder holds a file other than a kit's own that would be lost. Otherwise it makes the kit in brand/ again where it is, so it does not start while brand/ holds a file named like a kit's own, in any letter case, that its brand.json does not list.

source.description: The product's website, like https://linear.app, or a film.json you already have, so the pictures match that film. Given the website, it plans a film first with the default look, length and aspect; stills/ goes next to the film.json. The address needs a dot in its host name, so localhost on its own is refused.

wait_seconds.description: How long to wait for the result, counted from the start of the call, before returning a job_id to wait on. Some clients end a call after 60 or 240 seconds; 45 is safe in all of them.
